newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan army kills seven Tamil rebels in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan army kills seven Tamil rebels in ambush.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops ambushed and killed seven Tamil Tiger rebels in the eastern Trincomalee district, a Defence Ministry statement said on Thursday.

The statement said that rebel radio taffic monitored by the army indicated 10 guerrillas had been seriously wounded in the clash at Morawewa, about 240 km (150 miles) northeast of Colombo, on Wednesday.
The statment made no mention of casualties among the troops.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels killed 28 servicemen in two attacks in eastern Sri Lanka on Sunday.
The rebels' official Voice of Tigers radio said in a news broadcast on Monday that Sunday's attacks should be a reminder to the Sri Lankan government of their fighting ability.
The radio said the attacks disproved comments by Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte on the same day about ending the ethnic war before the year was over.

The Tigers, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, killed 22 soldiers and six policemen when they ambushed an army patrol and attacked a police post in Trincomalee district on Sunday.
The radio said two rebels were killed while trying to stop reinforcements from reaching the patrol which was ambushed.
The government says more than 50,000 have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
